harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created the appworker account on node1 and configured nofile=8192 / nproc=256 login-session limits via /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf, implemented as an Ansible playbook (playbook.yml + inventory.ini) run from node2 (control node, has ansible-core 2.20 installed). Since node1 (Ubuntu 16.04, Python 3.5) is incompatible with ansible-core 2.20's Python-module requirements, the playbook uses idempotent `raw` tasks (SSH-only, no target Python dependency) to create the user and write the limits file. Verified via a real SSH login session as appworker that both soft/hard nofile=8192 and soft/hard nproc=256 are enforced. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured healthy baselines, restarted node1 and node2 one at a time via `shutdown -r now`/`reboot`, confirmed changed boot_id on each, and verified post-restart recovery (user/limits persisted on node1, enforced via live SSH session; ansible-playbook re-run on node2 showed changed=0, confirming idempotent, working control-node tooling).
actions_performed: Identified node2 as the Ansible control node (has ansible-core 2.20 installed) and node1 (Ubuntu 16.04) as the target
Wired passwordless SSH (cluster keypair) from node2 to node1 as user 'antrieb' with passwordless sudo
Discovered node1's Python 3.5 is incompatible with ansible-core 2.20 modules (Python 3.8+ required); rewrote playbook using ansible.builtin.raw tasks
Created /root/ansible-appworker/{inventory.ini,playbook.yml} on node2 targeting node1
Ran ansible-playbook to create appworker user and write /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf with soft/hard nofile=8192 and soft/hard nproc=256
Re-ran playbook to confirm idempotency (changed=0)
Verified enforced limits via a live SSH login session as appworker (ulimit -Hn/-Sn/-Hu/-Su = 8192/8192/256/256), then cleaned up the temporary test SSH key
Captured pre-restart baselines (boot_id, uptime, user/limits state) on node1 and node2
Restarted node1 via 'shutdown -r now', polled until SSH returned, confirmed boot_id changed, verified appworker user/limits file intact, and re-verified live enforced limits via SSH login session
Restarted node2 via 'reboot', polled until SSH returned, confirmed boot_id changed, re-ran ansible-playbook (changed=0) confirming control-node tooling and node1 state fully recovered

evidence.summary: ansible-playbook run created the user; id appworker confirms uid=1001(appworker) exists

evidence.requirement: login-session limits of 8192 open files and 256 processes for appworker
evidence.summary: Playbook wrote /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf with soft/hard nofile 8192 and soft/hard nproc 256; live SSH login session as appworker shows ulimit -Hn/-Sn=8192/8192 and -Hu/-Su=256/256
ansible-playbook executed from node2 (control node) against node1 target using inventory.ini/playbook.yml; second run shows changed=0 confirming idempotent Ansible-managed state
Captured boot_id 8336c3a1... and confirmed appworker user + limits file present pre-restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: shutdown -r now acknowledged before disconnect; SSH connection refused confirms disruption; boot_id changed to 463c248a... after reconnect

evidence.requirement: node1 recovered state and data after restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart id/limits file intact; live SSH login session re-confirms enforced limits 8192/8192/256/256
Captured boot_id 416c5cf5... and confirmed ansible-core 2.20.5 functional pre-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: reboot acknowledged before disconnect; connection timeout confirms disruption; boot_id changed to 14e14fd7... after reconnect

evidence.requirement: node2 recovered state and control-node tooling after restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart ansible-playbook re-run succeeds with changed=0 (idempotent), proving control node and managed node1 state both fully recovered
